landmarks.name: Camp Dubois
landmarks.desc: The Corps' winter camp at the mouth of the Missouri. The journey begins.

landmarks.name: St. Charles
landmarks.desc: The last French village of any size on the river. Lewis joins the Corps here.

landmarks.name: Fire Prairie
landmarks.desc: Clark marks a commanding bluff as a fine place for a fort.

options.name: Up the Missouri
options.desc: Pole and tow the keelboat against the current. Slow, steady, safe.

options.name: Overland Trail
options.desc: Hunters march the prairie while the boats follow. Faster, but it wears the men down.

landmarks.name: Council Bluff
landmarks.desc: The first council with the Otoe and Missouria.

landmarks.name: Floyd's Bluff
landmarks.desc: Where Sergeant Charles Floyd was buried.

landmarks.name: Calumet Bluff
landmarks.desc: Council with the Yankton Sioux beneath the bluff.

landmarks.name: Mouth of the Bad River
landmarks.desc: The Teton Sioux under Black Buffalo hold the river here.

options.name: Main Channel
options.desc: Push straight up the main channel before the cold sets in.

options.name: Hug the Banks
options.desc: Slower going close to shore, with good hunting along the way.

landmarks.name: Knife River Villages
landmarks.desc: The busy earth-lodge towns of the Mandan and Hidatsa.

landmarks.name: Fort Mandan
landmarks.desc: The Corps' winter fort across the river from the villages.

options.name: Up the Missouri
options.desc: The keelboat goes home; the Corps moves on in pirogues and dugouts.

options.name: Overland March
options.desc: Cut across the plains and meet the canoes upriver.

landmarks.name: Yellowstone Confluence
landmarks.desc: Where the Yellowstone joins the Missouri. Game everywhere.

landmarks.name: The White Cliffs
landmarks.desc: Wind-carved sandstone Lewis called 'scenes of visionary enchantment'.

options.name: River Trail
options.desc: Tow the canoes through the shallows.

options.name: Bluff Shortcut
options.desc: Climb over the breaks and save days at a cost.

landmarks.name: Marias River
landmarks.desc: Two rivers of equal size. Which one is the Missouri?

landmarks.name: The Great Falls
landmarks.desc: Five cascades and an eighteen-mile portage.

landmarks.name: White Bear Islands
landmarks.desc: The portage's end, and grizzly country.

options.name: Canoes Upriver
options.desc: Paddle and pole through the Gates of the Mountains.

options.name: March the Bank
options.desc: Walk ahead of the canoes, hoping to find the Shoshone sooner.

landmarks.name: Three Forks
landmarks.desc: The Missouri divides into three rivers.

landmarks.name: Beaverhead Rock
landmarks.desc: Sacagawea recognises the land of her people.

landmarks.name: Lemhi Pass
landmarks.desc: The Continental Divide — and endless mountains beyond.

options.name: Guided Trail
options.desc: Follow a Shoshone guide along the trail the people use.

options.name: Ridge Route
options.desc: Strike out alone along the high ridges.

landmarks.name: Travelers' Rest
landmarks.desc: The last camp before the mountain crossing.

landmarks.name: Lolo Pass
landmarks.desc: Early snow, no game, and a trail that is hard to follow.

landmarks.name: Weippe Prairie
landmarks.desc: The starving Corps comes out of the mountains among the Nez Perce.

options.name: Dugouts Downriver
options.desc: Burn out dugout canoes and ride the Clearwater, Snake, and Columbia.

options.name: Run the Rapids
options.desc: Shoot the rapids rather than portage around them.

landmarks.name: Celilo Falls
landmarks.desc: The great fishing and trading place of the river peoples.

landmarks.name: Cape Disappointment
landmarks.desc: The Pacific Ocean at last.

landmarks.name: Fort Clatsop
landmarks.desc: A wet winter fort near the Clatsop people.
